method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the part into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: The pledge: worship God alone, be good to parents, relatives, orphans and the poor, speak well; yet they turned away, drove their own from their homes, and believed part of the Book while disbelieving part.
ideas: A modest kitchen table where parents, an orphan and a poor man are each served a bowl
A hand on a thin child's shoulder at a door
Suitcases piled on a curb outside a front door while a neighbor looks away
A line of people with bundles walking away from shut houses
A book with half its pages ripped out and blown away

sections.meaning: Messenger after messenger came, and whenever one came with what their souls did not desire they were arrogant; they said their hearts were wrapped.
ideas: A visitor's shadow on frosted glass and a man inside with his back turned and arms folded
A person wrapped head to toe in a heavy blanket in a bright room
A row of closed doors along a corridor

sections.meaning: When a Book came that confirmed what they had, and what they had long awaited arrived, they disbelieved it out of resentment, believing only what was sent to them.
ideas: A man who waited on a platform turns his back as a bright train arrives
A guest long expected arrives at a gate and the host shuts it
A man on a bench ignoring the sunrise he waited all night for

sections.meaning: They said 'we hear and we disobey', and the calf was made to sink into their hearts.
ideas: A man cups a hand to his ear toward a clear bell while his body walks away
Someone nods yes while his shoes point the other way

sections.meaning: If the home of the hereafter were theirs alone they would wish for death, but they never do; they are the most eager of people for life, each wanting a thousand years.
ideas: An old man at a table before a cake with a thousand candles
An old man clutching a clock to his chest on a bench
A man gripping a cliff ledge with both hands

sections.meaning: They make covenants and a group of them throws them away; they threw the Book of God behind their backs as if they did not know.
ideas: A man tosses a heavy book over his shoulder behind him as he walks on
A torn covenant paper fluttering into a river
A closed book left in the rain on a park bench

sections.meaning: They followed what the devils recited, magic that separates a man from his spouse; they bought what harms them and does not benefit them, but being mindful of God would have been better.
ideas: A kitchen table with a crack down the middle and two chairs turned away
A wedding ring on a floor in a crack of boards
Two coffee cups on a table before empty chairs

candidates.principle: And when we took the pledge of the Children of Israel: "You shall worship none but God, and do good to parents, and to relatives, orphans and the destitute, and say what is good to people, and keep up the prayer and give the alms." Then ...
candidates.shows: At a modest kitchen table, a woman serves a bowl of soup each to an old couple, a small child on her own and a poor man in worn clothes.
candidates.prompt: At a modest kitchen table in warm light, a woman in plain clothes ladles soup into bowls for an old couple, a small child sitting alone, and a poor man in worn coat, all seated around the same table with bread in the middle. The people are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.
